title: Spend limits
goal: Unified tracking for every model call (the chat agent, the case file classifier and categorizer, re-typing a file), each priced by what the AI Gateway billed for it; and usage limits by spend (USD), not token counts, because cost is the proper limit.
for_whom: A practising lawyer on a plan, who needs a fair allowance and a clear warning before it runs out; and platform staff, who need spend per lawyer that matches the gateway's bill.

done_check.check: Every AI Gateway model call is one usage_events row with a model and a cost: on the brief's database, one chat turn and one case upload (classify, categorize) and one re-type give exactly as many llm rows as gateway generations, each with cost_usd set and the user attributed. The decision-model classifier calls, missing on dev today (0 classify rows in 30 days), are among them.

A call whose reply carries no billed cost (a chat step cut off by the stop button, a gateway reply without cost) is still recorded and priced from the gateway (its generation record, else tokens x the /v1/models price list), marked estimated.

Two plan limits, 'Spend a day' and 'Spend a month' (USD, reset at Sri Lanka midnight and on the 1st), replace 'Context a day' and 'Context a month'; Free is $0.20 a day and $2 a month. Spend is the sum of cost_usd of the user's llm rows of every task (chat, file processing, re-type). Messages a day, searches a day, files per case and storage stay as they are.

Spend is checked before a chat turn, a case upload and a re-type; once an allowance is used, each is refused with a plain message saying which allowance and when it resets. Work already started (a turn, a file's processing) finishes and counts, even past the limit.
The lawyer sees only percent of allowance: /usage bars and the chat hint from 80% show no money anywhere. Admin pages (Usage, a user, Plans) show and edit spend in USD.

Admin Usage shows, for the period, our ledger's model spend next to the AI Gateway's own report (/v1/report) and the difference; when the report is unavailable (not a Pro team, or an error) it says so instead.

scenarios.steps: A lawyer on Free asks several questions about their case until today's spend passes 80%.
scenarios.expect: A hint above the chat box says how much of today's allowance is used (percent, no money); /usage shows the same.

scenarios.steps: The same lawyer, past today's allowance, asks another question.
scenarios.expect: It is refused in plain words: today's allowance is used, it resets at midnight. Yesterday's history is unaffected.

scenarios.steps: A lawyer uploads a scanned plaint to a case; it is processed (read, typed, summarised).
scenarios.expect: The processing's model cost appears in that lawyer's spend on /usage (as percent) and in USD on their admin user page, attributed to the file.

scenarios.steps: Platform staff open Admin Usage for this month.
scenarios.expect: Our model spend total and the gateway's total side by side, with the difference.

out_of_scope: Pricing embeddings, OCR, Zilliz or storage into spend: they stay bounded by the existing caps (files per case, storage).
A new files-a-day or files-a-month limit.
Gateway-native budgets (one API key per lawyer).
Showing amounts to lawyers in USD or LKR.

decisions.note: Everything a lawyer causes counts toward their spend: chat and the processing of their files, not chat alone (user).
Spend a day + spend a month replace the token limits; message, search and cap limits stay; Free $0.20/day, $2/month (user).
Lawyers see percent of allowance, never money; admins see USD (user).

Our ledger is the source for limits, not the gateway's report: /v1/report is aggregated, asynchronous and Pro-only, and gateway budgets are per Vercel team member, not per end user; the per-call cost the gateway returns inline is the same figure, available at once. /v1/report is used only to reconcile (Vercel docs, checked 2026-11-12).
Non-gateway costs (bge-m3, OCR, Zilliz, R2) are not priced into spend; existing caps bound them (user).

One path for every model call (user): re-type is a normal categorizer call, not a pipeline run, so no separate capture or check; spend sums every llm row with no task list, and one checkSpend replaces checkTokens where model work starts.
Task tags stay, though measured on dev at >= $0.00015 per call, 23% of chat spend over 106 calls (avg surcharge $0.000308 on avg billed $0.001335) (user).

A cost the gateway did not return is looked up from /v1/generation (2, 4, 8 s), else priced at /v1/models list prices; a cut-off stream has no generation id (probe), so it is always the list price on rough tokens. The reconcile compares the same whole UTC days on both sides (the report's days).
Lawyers' usage.mine carries no money at all (percent of the allowance, computed on the server); plan_limits/user_limits.max became double precision for USD.

progress.note: Scoped with the user in three rounds; issue #48; branch app/spend-limits; Neon branch agent/spend-limits.

Built d1-d6: meterCall for every gateway call (estimated when no cost), spend/spend_month (migration 0010 on the brief's branch), checkSpend before chat, upload, re-type, percent-only /usage, admin USD, per-file spend, gateway reconcile; unit tests pass. Next: live check on the brief's database, then /validate.

Live check on the brief's database (test user, headed browser): a chat turn = 5 llm rows summing to the message's billed $0.0047262; an upload = Jev classify + reader rows, priced, user and file attached; a re-type = 1 file.retype row; a stop before the reply began wrote nothing (doStream rejected before the wrapper), fixed and rechecked (estimated, prompt only); a stop mid-turn = billed step 1 + estimated cut step 2. At 82% the chat hint and /usage show percent only (usage.mine and the page carry no amount); past the limit, chat, upload and re-type are all refused with the plain message. Admin: USD on the user page, spend per file, Plans 0.2 / 2; Admin Usage says the gateway report needs a paid Vercel plan (team is not Pro). Not checked: an OCR'd scanned PDF (text file used), the reconcile numbers against a live report (unavailable on this team). Next: /validate.
